mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations spike above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth rebounds above 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or unemployment falls below 5% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which increases input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or industrial production rebounds above trend within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL over two months signals a combination of monetary easing and falling inflation, which lowers real interest rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation rises above 3% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both RSAFS (personal savings) and PAYEMS (payroll employment) above their 12-month averages for three consecutive months signals increased household financial capacity and labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS both exceed 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or either series falls below trend within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied by UNRATE dynamics and PAYEMS growth) above its 5-year average for six months indicates a broader labor supply, which can support wage growth and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE trend and PAYEMS growth jointly imply LFPR > 5-year average for six months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered periods, or labor force participation reverts below the 5-year average within the next three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or housing starts fall below trend within two months.
